target_state: implemented staging handoff. The complete 19-instruction body is reconstructed, the two indirect transfers it dispatches are reproduced through a trampoline that places the member object in ECX the way the listing does, and every claim in the source is annotated with the instruction it came from. Nothing is named beyond the displacements the listing prints: the binary carries no MSVC RTTI, no decompilation exists for this VA (evidence.evidence.missing_sections names DECOMPILATION), and the receiver record is bounds_only. implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX (aliased into ESI at 0x005732f1 and released before both exits), and NOTHING else: no stack push anywhere in the 19 instructions, and a bare RET (0x0057332b, byte c3) with no immediate on the one path that returns to its own caller. ghidra_function records parameter_count 0 and the signature 'undefined FUN_005732f0(void)'.
implementation.return_type_caveat: Word is the width the machine fixes (abi.return_register EAX) with the C type chosen among the 32-bit possibilities; the record's own inference classifies the value as pointer-like (abi.return_semantics 'pointer_like_in_EAX'). See return_semantics below for the three paths.
implementation.receiver_model: a byte run with no named members. The machine-derived receiver record enumerates offsets [776, 780] = [0x308, 0x30c] through ECX with written_through 2 and bounds_only true, which is where the body was seen reaching and not which member is which, so the model addresses both by displacement and names neither.
implementation.dispatch_model: two VTABLE_SLOT transfers, both proven from the listing's own bytes: the object's leading word is the table (0x00573307 / 0x00573322, a bare MOV EAX,[ECX]) and the callee is the table word at displacement 0x4 (0x00573309 / 0x00573324). The second transfer is a tail jump (0x00573328) and is modelled as a return of the transfer's value. dispatch_slot() places the member object in ECX before the transfer, because a plain C++ call would put the enclosing receiver there instead.
implementation.dependency_note: the body has no direct callees, so there is nothing to declare extern in the header. The only dependency is the table word, which is a runtime value; the model test supplies the far side of the transfer as six real functions (the slot the listing dispatches to, plus five decoys) so the test can see and count every transfer.

mechanics.body_shape: alias the receiver out of ECX into ESI; for the member at receiver+0x308, and then for the member at receiver+0x30c, in that order: test the word against zero, skip the transfer when it is zero, otherwise clear the word to 0 FIRST and then transfer to the table word at displacement 0x4 of the object the word pointed at, with that object in ECX. The first transfer is a CALL and the second is a tail JMP, so on the second one the callee returns to this body's caller.
mechanics.path_1_both_null: 0x005732fb and 0x00573316 both taken. No transfer, no store, no memory access at all beyond the two reads. EAX is never written by this body on this path.
mechanics.path_2_first_only: 0x005732fd clears receiver+0x308, 0x0057330c transfers into the object it named, 0x00573316 jumps to 0x0057332a, 0x0057332b returns. EAX is the first transfer's return value.
mechanics.path_3_second_taken: 0x00573318 clears receiver+0x30c and 0x00573328 tail-transfers into the object it named, so the body never executes its own RET on this path. EAX is the second transfer's return value, whatever the first one returned.

receiver_displacement.0x308: read at 0x005732f3 (MOV ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x308]) and written at 0x005732fd (MOV dword ptr [ESI + 0x308],0x0). Read once, never re-read: the value is consumed by the transfer at 0x0057330c, which is why clearing the field does not affect the object that transfer names.
receiver_displacement.0x30c: read at 0x0057330e and written at 0x00573318, on the same terms. The two words are adjacent dwords; nothing in the listing says they are related, and nothing says they are not.

mechanics.branch_conditions: two, both TEST reg,reg / JZ, i.e. equality against zero and nothing else. No range, alignment, type or plausibility test exists in the body: any non-null word transfers, and only a null word does not.
mechanics.write_ordering: each clear precedes its own transfer (0x005732fd before 0x0057330c, 0x00573318 before 0x00573328) and neither clear touches the other member. The ordering is observable from inside the callee and the model test observes it there.
mechanics.two_level_load: per member: MOV EAX,[ECX] then MOV EDX,[EAX+0x4]. The first load has NO displacement, the second has 0x4. Neither is the other's level: reading the member's value as a table, or the table's own leading word as the callee, are both refuted by the model test's decoys.
mechanics.not_modelled: the PUSH/POP of ESI (the C++ compiler preserves ESI as callee-saved, and the model test measures that it survives), the exact ESP the callee sees on the tail path, and the value the dynamic callee leaves in EAX beyond the fact that it leaves one.
mechanics.globals: none. The complete 19-instruction listing names no data-segment address and no absolute operand outside the body.

return_semantics.kind: machine-unfixed; the source declares a 32-bit word
return_semantics.value: the body's own RET path returns the FIRST transfer's EAX; its tail path returns the SECOND transfer's EAX straight to the caller; and on the path where both members are null it returns whatever EAX held on entry, because the listing writes EAX nowhere on that path. The declared type is therefore the width, not a type: the record's own inference RT2 classifies the last EAX write as pointer_like, but the value is a dynamic callee's return and this listing never shows what that callee returns.
return_semantics.source_choice: Word, chosen so the tail transfer's propagation is visible in the model and in the model test. kEaxUnwrittenOnTheNoMemberPath is the documented placeholder the model returns on the no-member path, where the machine fixes no value at all; the model test pins that placeholder and labels the check as a check on the model rather than evidence about the binary.
return_semantics.ownership: the body takes both members out of the receiver (each clear precedes its transfer) and hands each to a callee it does not own. Whether the callee releases them, and whether the receiver is expected to be refilled afterwards, is not observable from this listing: no body on the far side of either transfer is in evidence.
return_semantics.lifetime: the two member objects outlive the call if their callees keep them; the receiver's words do not, because both are 0 when the body returns.

observed_mechanics: 19 instructions, 0x005732f0..0x0057332b; no direct transfer, two indirect ones.
Receiver in ECX, aliased into ESI at 0x005732f1; the PUSH/POP of ESI exists because ECX is the callee-side receiver register for both transfers.
Reads the word at receiver+0x308; TEST/JZ against zero; on non-null clears the word to 0 and transfers to the table word at displacement 0x4 of the object it named, with that object in ECX.
Reads the word at receiver+0x30c and does the same thing, in that order.
The second transfer is a tail jump (0x00573328) after the frame word is popped, so its callee returns to this body's caller.
Both clears precede their own transfer; neither touches the other member.
On the path where both words are null the body reads four words, stores nothing and transfers nothing, and never writes EAX.
Return paths: the RET path yields the first transfer's EAX; the tail path yields the second's.
Machine dispatch record counts 2 indirect calls and 0 vtable-shaped loads; the listing shows two VTABLE_SLOT sites at slot displacement 0x4, and the listing governs.
The body is a table entry: the single xref is the data word 0x013f5844, displacement 0x4c of the 29-slot table at 0x013f57f8, and there are no direct callers.
semantic_findings: The body is a take-and-clear pair: each member is removed from the receiver and handed to a virtual call, and the removal happens before the call, not after it.

Both halves are the same shape and the same slot displacement, so this is one idiom applied twice rather than two different operations -- but the listing does not say the two members are the same KIND of thing, and the model does not claim it.
The prologue's register shuffle is not bookkeeping: ECX is the receiver register of both transfers, which is what forces the incoming receiver into ESI.
The second transfer is a tail jump, so on that path the body contributes no frame of its own to the callee and the callee's return value is this body's return value.

The member objects are polymorphic: their leading word is dereferenced to reach a table, and only the word at table displacement 0x4 is used. How many slots those tables have, and what slot 0x4 does, is not in evidence.

The body cannot be a static pass on RETURN SEMANTICS against this target's own record: the record's canonical return claim is the string 'pointer_like_in_EAX', which no C++ return type can equal, and the machine genuinely leaves the no-member path's EAX unwritten.

unresolved_questions: What class owns the receiver, and what are the two members? The image carries no MSVC RTTI (the word below the table at 0x013f57f8 is 0), the record has no SDK name for this VA, and no decompilation exists, so this package names nothing and asserts no member role.

What is at table displacement 0x4 of those member objects -- how many slots their tables have, and what the callee does. The slot word is loaded from memory at run time and no body on the far side of it is in evidence, so the callee's argument count, return type and effect are all unobserved.

What is the return type? The width is fixed (EAX, 32 bits) and the record classifies the value as pointer-like, but the C type is a source-side choice and the no-member path's EAX is never written by this body at all.

What is the ESP the callee sees on the tail path? The machine pops the frame word at 0x00573327 before jumping, so the callee resumes on this body's caller's stack; the model expresses the same transfer as a return, so its callee is entered with the model's frame still live. Nothing in the listing fixes the callee's stack, and no check in the model test pretends to.

Is the receiver refilled after the transfer? Both members are 0 when the body returns, and whether the object is re-armed afterwards is a question about the callee and about the owner of the receiver, neither of which is in this listing.

Why does abi_derived.dispatch record vtable_shaped_loads 0 for a body with two textbook two-level loads? The count disagrees with the listing's own bytes; the listing governs and the model depends on nothing in that record, but the detector's miss is unexplained.

Are the two members the same kind of thing? The two halves of the body are the same shape and the same slot displacement, which is suggestive and is not a claim; nothing in the listing relates the two words to each other.
